habitat: Long grass and bracken on hillsides, and open streams away from hills. It usually skulks, and sometimes perches on a tall stem.
summary: A common endemic resident. It has a rusty cap, heavily marked upperparts, streaked underparts except in the eastern race, black malar streaks, and a long rufous tail with straggly feathers. The song is a burst, 'chirp-chirp-chirp does it tickle yoooou', and it also mews. There is no Kemp estimate.

head.pattern: Rusty cap and black malar streaks.

upperparts.pattern: Heavily marked upperparts and a generally rusty colour.

underparts.pattern: Streaked underparts, except the eastern race.

viewNotes.note: Rusty cap, black malar streaks and a long straggly rufous tail.
Streaked underparts, except the eastern race.
Flight plumage is not described apart from the long tail.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: A burst of song, 'chirp-chirp-chirp does it tickle yoooou', and a cat-like mew. The grade A song is from Cape Point. The filename is CapeGrassbirdCapePoint2006-12-27.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common endemic resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Rusty is not a colour name, so the cap colour is left unset. There is no Kemp estimate. No Kruger photograph was found. The grade A song is from Cape Point and is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.

population.notes: No sourced Kruger estimate is currently available; taxonomy or later records require separate research.
